precepts.text: Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me. Disobeying the commandments demonstrates that you hate God.
precepts.point: Moses bowed and said, if I have found grace, go among us, for it is a stiffnecked people, and pardon our iniquity and take us for thine inheritance. Stiffnecked then, the same hard heads today. The elect are the men and women who fit within the escape he created; do not get pulled off your game by slick talk.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will “by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.” Exodus 20:5 shows who that is spoken of: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”

Of them that hate me. To disobey God's commandments is to demonstrate that you hate God. He pardons iniquity and transgression and sin, but if we are guilty of breaking his laws, we are going to pay.

That is why this is read in the wilderness, right after the commandments and statutes were given. A lot of us did not learn from the mistakes we made back then. We came back and did the same damn thing, still wicked and evil and covetous to this day, and the Most High is going to keep sending those afflictions until the lesson is learned. Read the book of your fathers to find out what we did and why all this hell is on us, and you will know what not to do today.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, wife, manservant, maidservant, ox, ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's. Covet means to take what does not belong to you by deceit. The same covetousness from back then is still practised today.
precepts.point: Moses bowed and said, if I have found grace, go among us, for it is a stiffnecked people, and pardon our iniquity and take us for thine inheritance. Stiffnecked then, the same hard heads today. The elect are the men and women who fit within the escape he created; do not get pulled off your game by slick talk.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
The iniquity visited upon the children in Exodus 34:7 is the same sin carried from generation to generation, and covetousness is one of them. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.”

To covet means to take what does not belong to you: to take it by wickedness, by deceit. The same BS we were doing back then, we still do today, coveting our neighbour's house and our neighbour's wife.

Then, “nor his ox”: hold it right there. That points to Exodus 22, the same chapter Negroes use to beguile you sisters. The whole of that chapter is about thou shalt not covet. Then, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”: you are not supposed to covet, to take, anything that belongs to that father, that neighbour.

So the iniquity of the fathers that is still being visited on us is the same covetousness, and we should learn not to carry that evil all the way up to now.

precepts.text: Steal an ox and you restore five oxen: the whole chapter restrains covetousness, like a speeding ticket raising your insurance. If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, he coveted her behind her father's back, broke the tenth commandment, and the father can refuse him. Dinah was spoken to sweetly, not raped, and her brothers still would not give her. No backdoor marriages will be approved; if a sister has to be snatched out and sit with that scarlet letter, it is better than being tied to a man who went behind her father's back.
precepts.point: Moses bowed and said, if I have found grace, go among us, for it is a stiffnecked people, and pardon our iniquity and take us for thine inheritance. Stiffnecked then, the same hard heads today. The elect are the men and women who fit within the escape he created; do not get pulled off your game by slick talk.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Exodus 22 is the law put in place for those that wanted to do evil, and it is proper. The whole chapter is about putting restraints on covetousness. It is not telling you how you are supposed to move. It is like a speeding ticket: your insurance goes way up, and that is the consequence of breaking the original law. Drive the damn speed limit.

“If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That is covetousness: you coveted thy neighbour's ox, exactly what Exodus 20:17 forbids. If you do, you pay for the one you stole and give him five oxen for it.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” The maid belongs to her father. To entice her means you coveted to get her; you did it behind the father's back, in deceit. You broke the tenth commandment, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” You lured her away from her father, and you are going to try to tell me that is righteous? You are a damn fool. And a woman that has no wisdom will follow that and pay for the judgment.

Verse 17 kills it: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father said hell no. Even though you enticed her, you are not taking her. That is what happened with Dinah: she was enticed, spoken to sweetly and kindly; she was not raped. Even though he wanted to marry her, her brothers said no, snatched her out of that house, and she had to sit there defiled.

That should be a warning to you women. No backdoor marriages will be approved, period. If we have to snatch you out, and you have to sit with that scarlet letter knowing you were defiled, that is better than being tied up with somebody that means you pure evil. How could you even respect a man who went behind your father's back, your protection's back? This is the guilty that Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will by no means clear.

precepts.text: Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and to the fourth generation.
precepts.point: The man born blind was not paying for his own sin; God used him to show his power. Do not presume on God's mercy and play with his judgment.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 makes it super clear. The Lord is “Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty”. The guilty were those that killed the prophets. He is “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation”.

The iniquity of the fathers was the murder of the prophets, and it was visited upon the children, the Pharisees of Christ's day. That is what Christ meant by “Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers”: you were your fathers, doing the killing back then. Those born in the third and fourth generation pay for the sins committed three or four generations ago.

So the man born blind in John 9 was not paying for his own sin. The Most High caused him to be born blind so that he could be healed later, and the Lord may allow a situation anywhere so he can exercise his mercy and his power on it as an example to the rest of us. People needed to see that Christ could heal. The Lord has people's lives plotted out for what he needs them to be.

But that is not an excuse to do evil. Don't be so confident in his mercy that you go out and play with the Most High's judgment, because he will by no means clear the guilty, and you might not even make it in here.

precepts.text: Destroy all the places where the nations served their gods, under every green tree.
precepts.point: Groves of trees are where the nations worshipped, and powerful men still gather at such places.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Our commandment from our God was to destroy their altars, break their images and cut down their groves. A grove is trees, and they were cut down because they were sacred trees. Moses gives the same command in Deuteronomy: “Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods”. Destroy the places where the nations served their gods, wherever they are.

Watch where those places were: “upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree”. Not some trees. Under every green tree: evergreen, oak, cedar, palm, pine. Any place they served gods on a high mountain or a high hill, destroy it, and every place under a green tree, destroy it.

Read verse 3 and the command goes further: “And ye shall overthrow their altars, and break their pillars, and burn their groves with fire”. Burn the groves with fire. The Bohemian Grove, where most of the presidents, if not all of them, have gone, has an idol of Molech, the owl, standing under trees so tall all you see is the stalk. Don't focus on the owl; look at what surrounds it. The idol is under the tree. If we were in power today, that owl would be destroyed and those trees burned all around it. Burn it all.

That is why the tree matters for Exodus 34:13. The groves Israel was told to cut down are the trees the heathen worship under, and the tree set up in the house at Christmas is the same thing.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

Why under the trees? “because the shadow thereof is good”. That owl in the Bohemian Grove sits under the shadow of those trees in the picture. The shadow of the tree is good to them because the idol is under the tree.

Then the fruit of it: “therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your spouses shall commit adultery”. Around that owl they visit, they do all kinds of sexual rituals; sexual things take place around that owl at Bohemian Grove. All the presidents, including Obama, who y'all love so much, went there, and who knows what was going on over there.

So the groves were not harmless. The worship under the green tree brings whoredom and adultery with it, and that is why God commanded Israel to cut them down.

precepts.text: Under every green tree, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols.
precepts.point: Groves of trees are where the nations worshipped, and powerful men still gather at such places.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Ezekiel names the same places: “upon every high hill, in all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols”. Under every green tree and under every thick oak, that is where they offered to their idols. Where did they sacrifice? Under the tree.

And God's judgment falls right there: “Then shall ye know that I am the Lord, when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars”. The slain lie among the idols and around the altars under the trees.

Now see what the sacrifice is called. Matthew 5:23: “Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar”, and “Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift”. The gift is the sacrifice. Matthew 8:4 says the same: “offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them”. Moses commanded a gift, a sacrifice.

So when the heathen sacrificed under their tree, what was under the tree? Gifts. You don't put gifts on top of the tree, beside the tree, or hang them on the tree. You put them under the tree. That is where it comes from: the gifts under the Christmas tree are the heathen's offering to their idols under every green tree.

precepts.text: Who maketh the clouds his chariot; the cloud the Lord descended in is His vehicle of travel.
precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“And the Lord descended in the cloud, and stood with him there”. “Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind”.

The clouds are His chariot, His vehicle, His way of traveling. The cloud the Lord descended in on the mount is His vehicle of travel; the Most High, Christ and the angels travel in these vehicles.

precepts.text: I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee; thou canst not see my face and live; Moses stood upon the rock, was covered in the clift, and saw the back parts.
precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
On the mount the Lord “proclaimed the name of the Lord”, as He had promised Moses: “I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy.”

No man can see the face of the Most High and live: “Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.” So the Lord set Moses upon a rock, put him “in a clift of the rock”, and covered him with His hand while His glory passed by. “And I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.” Moses saw only His back parts, and the proclamation of Exodus 34 is the keeping of that promise.

precepts.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob; he hath not dealt so with any nation. The forgiveness proclaimed here belongs to Israel.
precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin”: this is spoken to Israel. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them.”

Moses is speaking only to the children of Israel at this time. The word and the statutes were given to Israel only, so the forgiveness proclaimed on the mount belongs to Israel.

precepts.text: Sin is the transgression of the law; the sin being forgiven is the breaking of the law given to Israel.
precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” The sin being forgiven, “forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin”, is the breaking of the law given to Israel.

The word and the statutes were given to Israel only, so this mercy is spoken to Israel. And it does not clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged, “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.”

precepts.text: The dead bodies in the street of the great city spiritually called Sodom and Egypt are Israel spiritually dead in captivity; the Spirit of life enters them, they stand upon their feet, and great fear falls on them which see them. This is the marvel the Most High spoke of.
precepts.point: They that dwell upon the earth rejoiced over them, made merry, and sent gifts one to another, because these had tormented them. Then the Spirit of life from God entered into them: the people that were spiritually dead in captivity, that would not look their slave masters in the face, stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them which saw them; that same fear falls on the slave masters.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
The Most High made a covenant to do marvels “such as have not been done in all the earth, nor in any nation”, and “all the people among which thou art shall see the work of the Lord”. One of those marvels is laid out in the Revelation.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” Israel lay as dead bodies in that street: a decayed state, a spiritually dead people. “they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies” through the years of captivity, when they were slaves, and they “shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves”, because the death is spiritual, not physical. The two witnesses go to the northern and southern kingdoms.

“they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them”. Then “the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” The people that were spiritually dead in captivity, that would not look their slave masters in the face, stand upon their feet, and that same fear falls on the slave masters. That is the terrible thing the Lord said He would do with Israel, before all the people.

precepts.text: Destroy their altars, break down their images, and cut down their groves; the command of this chapter is written again in the law.
precepts.point: The snare is spelled out: they go a whoring after their gods, they call thee, thou eat of their sacrifice and partake in serving their gods; thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“But ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves”. The law states it again: “thus shall ye deal with them; ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.”

The Most High drives out the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, and the command in both places is the same: no covenant with the inhabitants of the land, “lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee”, and nothing of their worship left standing, “For thou shalt worship no other god: for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God”.

precepts.text: Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the LORD in the place which he shall choose, at the three feasts, and they shall not appear before the LORD empty.
precepts.point: Neither shall any man desire thy land when thou shalt go up to appear before the Lord thrice in the year: when the men left their land and went up to keep the three high holy days, the Most High promised no man would desire their land.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Thrice in the year shall all your men children appear before the Lord God, the God of Israel.” The law is written again in Deuteronomy, and it names the three: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles”.

The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover season; the feast of weeks is Pentecost; and the feast of ingathering at the year's end is the feast of tabernacles. “and they shall not appear before the Lord empty”: each had to bring his sacrifice.

When the men left their land and went up to keep the three high holy days, the Most High promised, “neither shall any man desire thy land, when thou shalt go up to appear before the Lord thy God thrice in the year.”

precepts.text: A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed; that is why Moses' face shone.
precepts.point: Moses put a vail on his face until he had done speaking with the people; but when he went in before the Lord to speak with Him he took the vail off, to show respect to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.”

That is why the skin of Moses' face shone when he came down from mount Sinai, and he wist it not. This was no ordinary wisdom Moses was getting; he was getting the utmost wisdom, and it made his face shine so that Aaron and all the children of Israel were afraid to come nigh him.

precepts.text: The Most High shewed Moses the secrets of the times and the end; that measure of wisdom made his face shine, and some of it he was commanded to hide.
precepts.point: Moses put a vail on his face until he had done speaking with the people; but when he went in before the Lord to speak with Him he took the vail off, to show respect to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
The Most High tells what Moses received in the mount: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”.

He saw the beginning of the creation, the middle and the end of these times. That measure of wisdom is why his face shone, for a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine.

“These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” Some of that wisdom Moses was commanded to hide and not declare; there is wisdom the Most High gave him that he was not to publish, that we do not even have right now.

precepts.text: The Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children.
precepts.point: The judgment of David was that child being put to death. This goes back to Exodus 34: the Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquities of the fathers upon the children. David got pardoned, but he did not get cleared; the punishment was still coming, one part the men of Israel dying in battle, the other his son having to die and his house having nothing but trouble.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

precepts.why:
The Most High is “Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children”.

David confessed, “I have sinned against the Lord.” Nathan answered, “The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die. Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.”

That is both halves of Exodus 34:7. David got pardoned, but he did not get cleared. The punishment was still coming: one part the men of Israel dying in battle, the other his son having to die and his house having nothing but trouble. The judgment of David was that child being put to death.

precepts.text: The Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children.
precepts.point: Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

precepts.why:
He is “Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children”.

David repented and was forgiven, yet the judgment spoken in chapter 12 still came to pass on the roof of his own house, when his son went in unto his concubines in the sight of all Israel. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty.

So even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

points: The Most High made a covenant to do marvels such as have not been done in all the earth, nor in any nation, and all the people among which Israel dwells shall see the work of the Lord. One of those marvels is laid out in the Revelation.
